sentences.text: The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar

Writ Petition No.44941 Of 2022
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed by the sixteen (16) petitioners questioning the action of the respondents in paying compensation only to an extent of Acs.12.29 gts. out of total extent of Acs.19.20 gts. situated in Sy.No.512 of Eliminedu Village, Ibrahimpatnam Mandal, Ranga Reddy District,
as illegal and arbitrary

. 
2. The brief facts, that are relevant for the disposal of the Writ Petition, are as under:-
3. Pursuant to a request made by respondent No.6 herein for acquiring the land situated in Sy.Nos.166, 421, 492 and 512 totally admeasuring Acs.572.15 gts. situated in Eliminedu Village,
Ibrahimpatnam Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, for the purpose of establishment of Industrial Park,
a preliminary notification under Section 11(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act, 2013'), was published vide proceedings No.G1/1162/2015, dated 28.03.2018, notifying the subject lands.

Thereafter, further proceedings pursuant to the said preliminary ::2::
MSK,J WP_44941_2022 notification have taken place.
But, the petitioners herein in all were paid compensation only to an extent of Acs.12.29 gts. as against the total extent of Acs.19.20 gts. being claimed by the petitioners.
4. Aggrieved by such non-payment of compensation to an extent of Acs.6.31 gts., the petitioners claim to have approached the respondents.
But, having not received any response, the petitioners approached this Court by filing the present Writ Petition.

5. Respondent No.3 filed a counter affidavit stating that, though the total land to an extent of Acs.19.20 gts. was notified for acquisition, after conducting an enjoyment survey, the petitioners were found to have been in possession and enjoyment of the land only to an extent of Acs.12.29 gts.
and as such, they were paid compensation for the said extent only and for the remaining extent of Acs.6.31 gts.,
the compensation was paid to the persons, who are in actual physical enjoyment of the said extent of land.

6. This Court, having not been able to convince about the stand of the respondents in paying compensation to the persons, who are stated to be in physical possession basing upon an enjoyment survey conducted by the respondents, called ::3::
Hanumanthu Chandraiah vs The State Of Telangana on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158558546/
1 MSK,J WP_44941_2022 upon the respondents to justify their action.

sentences.text: In response to the same, an additional counter affidavit was filed by respondent No.3 stating that after conducting an enjoyment survey in presence of the petitioners and other villagers, the petitioners have agreed to receive compensation only to an extent of Acs.12.29 gts.
and also agreed for apportionment of the said compensation among the petitioners, as such the petitioners are not entitled to agitate the issue before this Court.
It is also stated that the compensation that is payable in respect of Acs.6.31 gts. was paid in favour of the persons, who are in enjoyment of the said extent of land.
7. The concept of payment of compensation to the person in possession, while ignoring the claim of the person, who is having title over the said land, is totally unknown to law.

The basis for concluding that a particular person is in possession of the subject land under acquisition either prior to issuance of the preliminary notification or thereafter is a matter that is being verified by the officials of the Revenue department and there is no basis for arriving at such a conclusion, except the survey report or an enquiry report that is prepared or obtained during the acquisition proceedings.

Payment of compensation only basing upon such enjoyment survey cannot be accepted as ::4::
MSK,J WP_44941_2022 legal way of deciding the entitlement for payment of compensation.

An Employee or Officer of the Revenue department would be the person who conduct the so-called enjoyment survey and if whatever findings that are recorded by the said Survey Officer is to be taken as basis for payment of compensation for the land acquired, while ignoring the claim of the person, who has got title over the subject land, such an action is bound to be declared as arbitrary.

In case, if the Survey Officer, without there being any basis, in his discretion and as per his whims and fancies, submits a report that one 'X' is in possession of the subject property and if the compensation is to be paid to such 'X' basing upon such survey report, while ignoring the claim of the person, who is having title over the said extent of land, the very purpose of providing a mechanism for resolving the disputes with regard to claim for compensation or with regard to apportionment of the compensation, as provided under Sections 76 and 77 of the Act, 2013, read with Section 64 of the Act, 2013 would be futile.
Therefore, the contention of the respondents that the compensation in respect of Acs.6.31 gts. was paid in favour of the persons in enjoyment of the said extent of land is cannot be accepted.

MSK,J WP_44941_2022 8. Be that as it may, in the additional counter affidavit filed by respondent No.3 a serious dispute is raised about the entries that were made in the Revenue records and also about the assignments that were made in favour of the petitioners herein/their predecessor-in-title etc., in the considered view of this Court may require a detailed consideration and it is only after such consideration, the entitlement or otherwise of the petitioners for payment of compensation in respect of the said extent Hanumanthu Chandraiah vs The State Of Telangana on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158558546/
2 of Acs.6.31 gts. can be decided finally.
9.

sentences.text: In the additional counter affidavit filed by respondent No.3, it is also stated that the petitioners herein, having participated in the enjoyment survey, have agreed for payment of compensation only to an extent of Acs.12.29 gts. as against the total extent of Acs.19.21 gts.
and it is further stated that the petitioners have given an affidavit agreeing for such a process.
A copy of the said affidavit said to have been given by the petitioners is also placed on record.

A perusal of the same shows that petitioner Nos.1 to 14 and 16 have signed the said affidavit agreeing to receive the compensation to an extent of Acs.12.29 gts. and also for apportionment of the same among themselves.

Accordingly,
the compensation was stated to have been paid to petitioner Nos.1 to 14 and 16.

Petitioner No.15,
::6::
MSK,J WP_44941_2022 who is son of one Mr. Ramulu, is concerned, the mother of petitioner No.15 namely Mrs. Hanumanthu Andalu W/o Mr. Ramulu, was shown to have been paid compensation to an extent of Ac.0.13.05 gts.
10.
But, for the reasons best known, the petitioners suppressed before this Court the fact of giving such an affidavit.

In spite of filing an additional counter affidavit by respondent No.3, no reply affidavit is filed contradicting the averments contained in the said additional counter affidavit and also about the consent affidavit said to have been given by the petitioners herein.

The extents for which the petitioners were paid compensation, as shown in the said consent affidavit, are mostly tallying with the extent notified against the names of each of the petitioners in the declaration made under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013, vide proceedings No.G1/1162/2015, dated 01.04.2019,
published in Gazette No.RR.31, Ranga Reddy District, dated 01.04.2019.

Further, the petitioners,
who are claiming for payment of compensation in respect of their individual extents, have approached this Court by filing a common Writ Petition without furnishing any particulars of their respective entitlements, extents of land, the details of ::7::
MSK,J WP_44941_2022 assignment of the respective extents of land etc. thereby disabling this Court to examine the matter in detail.
11.
In the light of the above, this Court is not inclined to grant the relief as sought for in the Writ Petition.

However, in the considered view of this Court, the petitioners are entitled to agitate their claim for payment of compensation in respect of the extents, for which they were stated to have been denied compensation.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of giving liberty to the petitioners to submit individual claim petitions before respondent No.3, by narrating the basis for their claim

,
within a period of four (04) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and on submission of such individual claims of the petitioners, respondent No.3 is directed to refer the claims of the petitioners under Sections 76 and 77 of the Act, 2013, for adjudicating as to whether they are entitled for such compensation vis--vis the claim of the so-called enjoyers of the respective extents of land, within a further period of six (06) weeks from the date of receipt of such claims from the petitioners.

In case, if the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Authority (for short 'the LAR & R authority') comes to a conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for payment of any compensation, the same shall be ::8::
Hanumanthu Chandraiah vs The State Of Telangana on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158558546/
3 MSK,J WP_44941_2022 paid to the petitioners, without reference to the compensation already paid to the so-called enjoyers.

sentences.text: However, it is made clear, in such an event, it is open for the respondent-authorities to take steps for recovery of such amounts paid to the so-called enjoyers.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
No costs.

MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR, J Date:10.11.2023 NDS Hanumanthu Chandraiah vs The State Of Telangana on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158558546/
